name: Cassava Mealybug
description: A serious pest of cassava that sucks sap from growing tips, causing stunting, leaf distortion, and reduced root yield. It was accidentally introduced to Africa from South America and has been successfully controlled in many areas by biological control agents.
symptoms: White waxy masses on stem tips and leaf axils
Stunted shoot growth with shortened internodes
Severely stunted plants with bushy appearance
treatments: Apply systemic insecticides (imidacloprid) early in infestation
Spray neem oil or insecticidal soap to control crawlers
Prune and destroy heavily infested shoot tips
Introduce biological control agent Apoanagyrus lopezi (parasitoid wasp)
prevention: Establish and conserve Apoanagyrus lopezi populations in fields
Use clean stem cuttings from uninfested fields
Remove and destroy volunteer cassava plants between seasons
Monitor regularly for early signs of infestation
Avoid unnecessary insecticide use that kills parasitoids
references: IITA Cassava Mealybug Biological Control Guide
